<h>Lectio 1</h>
<r>1 Reg 1:20-22</r>
<n>20</n> Et factum est post círculum diérum, concépit Anna, et péperit fílium: vocavítque nomen eius Sámuel, eo quod a Dómino postulásset eum.
<n>21</n> Ascéndit autem vir eius Elcana, et omnis domus eius, ut immoláret Dómino hóstiam solémnem, et votum suum.
<n>22</n> Et Anna non ascéndit: dixit enim viro suo: Non vadam donec ablactétur infans, et ducam eum, ut appáreat ante conspéctum Dómini, et máneat ibi iúgiter.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Præparáte corda vestra Dómino, et servíte illi soli:
* Et liberábit vos de mánibus inimicórum vestrórum.
<r>℣.</r> Convertímini ad eum in toto corde vestro, et auférte deos aliénos de médio vestri.
<r>℟.</r> Et liberábit vos de mánibus inimicórum vestrórum.

<n>24</n> Et addúxit eum secum, postquam ablactáverat, in vítulis tribus, et tribus módiis farínæ, et ámphora vini, et addúxit eum ad domum Dómini in Silo.

b.eaf60f3f99:
<h>Oratio</h>
<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
<n><k>Pater Noster</k> dicitur secreto usque ad <k>Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:</k></n>
<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
<r>℣.</r> Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
<r>℟.</r> Sed líbera nos a malo.

<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>eus, in te sperántium fortitúdo, adésto propítius invocatiónibus nostris: et, quia sine te nihil potest mortális infírmitas, præsta auxílium grátiæ tuæ; ut, in exsequéndis mandátis tuis, et voluntáte tibi et actióne placeámus.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.c7a463e2e0:
<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, the Strength of all them that put their trust in thee, mercifully accept our prayers, and because through the weakness of our mortal nature we can do no good thing without thee, grant us the help of thy grace, that in keeping of thy commandments we may please thee, both in will and deed.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

b.c135788acf:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>S</c>éptimo Kaléndas Iúnii Luna vicésima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>R</h>omæ sancti Philíppi Nérii, Presbýteri et Confessóris, qui Congregatiónis Oratórii Fundátor fuit, ac virginitáte, prophetíæ dono, et miráculis éxtitit insígnis.
<h>I</h>tem Romæ sancti Eleuthérii, Papæ et Mártyris, qui multos nóbiles Romanórum ad fidem Christi perdúxit, et sanctos Damiánum et Fugátium in Británniam misit, qui Lúcium Regem, cum uxóre ipsíus ac toto fere pópulo, baptizárunt.
<h>C</h>antuáriæ, in Anglia, natális sancti Augustíni, Epíscopi et Confessóris; qui, una cum áliis, a beáto Gregório Papa missus, genti Anglórum sacrum Christi Evangélium prædicávit, ibíque, virtútibus et miráculis gloriósus, obdormívit in Dómino. Eius tamen festívitas quinto Kaléndas Iúnii recólitur.
<h>A</h>thénis item natális beáti Quadráti, Apostolórum discípuli, qui, in persecutióne Hadriáni, fide et indústria sua cóngregans Ecclésiam grandi terróre dispérsam, librum pro Christiánæ religiónis defensióne, valde útilem et Apostólica doctrína dignum, eídem Imperatóri porréxit.
<h>R</h>omæ sanctórum Mártyrum Simítrii Presbýteri, et aliórum vigínti duórum; qui sub Antoníno Pio passi sunt.
<h>V</h>iénnæ, in Gállia, sancti Zacharíæ, Epíscopi et Mártyris, qui sub Traiáno passus est.
<h>I</h>n Africa sancti Quadráti Mártyris, in cuius solemnitáte sanctus Augustínus sermónem hábuit.
<h>T</h>udérti, in Umbria, natális sanctórum Mártyrum Felicíssimi, Heráclii et Paulíni.
<h>I</h>n território Antisiodorénsi pássio sancti Prisci Mártyris, qui, cum ingénti multitúdine fidélium Christi, cápite cæsus est.
<h>I</h>n civitáte Quiténsi, Æquatoriánæ Ditiónis, sanctæ Maríæ Annæ a Iesu de Parédes, Vírginis, e tértio Ordine sancti Francísci, austeritáte et in próximum caritáte præcláræ, quam Pius Papa Duodécimus sanctárum Vírginum catálogo adnumerávit.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.830f80e6b1:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>M</c>ay 26th 2027, the 20th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:

<h>A</h>t Rome, holy Philip Neri, founder of the Congregation of the Oratory, famous for his virginity, his gift of prophecy, and his wondrous works.
<h>A</h>lso at Rome, the holy Pope and martyr Eleutherius, who led many noble Romans to believe in Christ, and who sent into Britain holy Dyfan and Ffagan, who baptized Lleurwg, Prince [of Morgan,] along with his wife and nearly all his people.
<h>I</h>n England, the holy Augustine, first Archbishop of Canterbury, called Apostle of England. He was sent hither, along with others, by the blessed Pope Gregory. He preached the Gospel of Christ to the English people. He fell asleep in the Lord at Canterbury, glorious for his graces and wondrous works.
<h>A</h>t Athens, the blessed Quadratus, a disciple of the Apostles. During the persecution under Hadrian the Church was scattered in great fear, but he gathered it together again by his faith and labour, and gave unto it a book very useful for the defending of the Christian religion, and worthy of the teaching of the Apostles.
<h>A</h>lso at Rome, the holy Priest Simitrius, and twenty-two others, who suffered martyrdom under the Emperor Antoninus Pius.
<h>A</h>t Vienne, in Dauphiny, the holy Zachary, Bishop [of that see,] who suffered martyrdom under Trajan.
<h>I</h>n Africa, the holy martyr Quadratus, on whose feast-day holy Augustine [of Hippo] preached a sermon.
<h>A</h>t Todi, [in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian,] the holy martyrs Felicissimus, Heraclius, and Paulinus.
<h>I</h>n the country of Auxerre, [in the second century,] the holy Priscus and a vast multitude of Christ's faithful people suffered martyrdom.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
